articles.title: Saka salutes Arsenal’s defensive resolve after hard-fought Villa win: ‘Without the ball we were incredible’
articles.summary: Bukayo Saka has hailed his Arsenal team-mates for their performance against Aston Villa.
articles.content:
Saka salutes Arsenal’s defensive resolve after hard-fought Villa win: ‘Without the ball we were incredible’

Bukayo Saka has hailed his Arsenal team-mates for their performance against Aston Villa.

Last Update:

Bukayo Saka has praised Arsenal’s defensive work as the foundation of their 1-0 win at Aston Villa on Bank Holiday Monday, insisting the champions showed exactly the kind of resilience required to mount a serious title defence.

Saka’s close-range finish just before the hour mark was the difference between the sides at Villa Park, the winger converting Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross after a slick move that released the pair of them in behind a high Villa line.

It was Arsenal’s second consecutive win and second consecutive clean sheet to open the new campaign, with Mikel Arteta marking his 250th Premier League game in charge of the club with maximum points.

“Very, very tough game. It’s not easy coming here, they made it hard for us. It feels even better to come out with the win,” Saka said.

“The way they defend, really compact and with a high line, they caught us offside. We had to adapt to that. Different from what we faced last week, we weren’t able to implement our attacking pattern.

“One goal is normally enough for us because we are so solid at the back. When we got the first one, it actually opened the game up. We wanted to push for the second one.”

The winger singled out Arsenal’s full-back play as a key contributor to their attacking threat, before returning to the theme of their defensive performance as the match’s defining feature.

“All the full-backs, the way they play gives us a lot. For us wingers, it opens up the game for us, we’ve always got composure in the box,” he said.

“We weren’t at our highest level with the ball. Without it, we were incredible. As soon as we lost it, we were running back. We knew that they liked to play in transition. All the boys put in a shift tonight. It helps with a clean sheet.”

Arteta on squad depth

Villa offered precious little in terms of attacking threat throughout, they have not registered a shot on target in either of their two opening Premier League fixtures, the first time any team has achieved that since Swansea City in 2017-18.

Arsenal, however, could not afford complacency against a side stung by the 4-0 defeat to Brighton on the opening weekend, and Arteta acknowledged as much.

“This is a really difficult place to come and win the game. Last season we lost in the last kick of the game. They were hurt after what happened last week. It was a great squad performance tonight,” he said.

Arteta was asked whether this represents his strongest-ever squad in terms of depth.

“That is what we need. The players that come in make the difference. All of them contributed to create more dominance and more momentum,” he said.

“The level of focus and the way they want to contribute to the team, that is going to be decisive in the season.”

Joao Pedro eyeing Brazil return after strong Chelsea start

Joao Pedro believes he's strong start to the season deserves a Brazil recall.

Last Update:

Joao Pedro is hoping his strong start to the season at Chelsea can earn him a regular place in Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad.

Ancelotti was in the stands at Stamford Bridge on Sunday to watch Joao Pedro start and score in Chelsea’s 4-3 win over Brighton.

The 24-year-old has now scored twice and provided two assists in his opening two Premier League games this season, continuing the impressive form he showed during his first campaign at Chelsea.

“I try to do my job regardless of who is watching,” Joao Pedro told ESPN after the game.

“I always aim to maintain a high standard. As for the Brazilian national team, I want to carry on doing my job and, God willing, I’ll be there.”

Joao Pedro was left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, with Ancelotti opting for more experienced attacking options.

The forward has eight caps for his country since making his senior debut in 2023 and is now hoping his performances for Chelsea can put him back in contention.

Pedro aiming for titles

Joao Pedro joined Chelsea from Brighton in July 2025 and enjoyed an impressive first season at Stamford Bridge, scoring 20 goals and providing nine assists in 50 appearances.

He was subsequently named Chelsea’s Player of the Season.

“I think I’ve been proving this [good form] over the years,” Joao Pedro said.

“I got off to a good start last season, and this season too; now it’s a case of keeping up the pace, carrying on working hard and, God willing, finishing as high up the table as possible.”

Brazil were eliminated by Norway in the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup and will return to action against Australia in a friendly on September 25.

articles.title: BREAKING: Lionel Messi retires from international football
articles.summary: Lionel Messi has retired from international football
articles.content:
BREAKING: Lionel Messi retires from international football

Lionel Messi has retired from international football

Last Update:

Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football with Argentina, saying the decision “hurt” but that he understands “the time has come”.

The 39-year-old ends his international career as Argentina’s record goalscorer and most-capped player, with 125 goals in 207 appearances.

Inter Miami striker Messi captained Argentina to World Cup glory while he was a Paris Saint-Germain player in 2022 and led his country to the 2026 final, losing 1-0 to Spain after extra time in New Jersey on August 19.

Lionel Messi: Argentina icon’s full retirement statement

“After all this time that has passed since the final, and after much thought, I want to announce to everyone that I am retiring from the national team,” Messi said.

“It was a decision that hurt – and still hurts – to my core, but I understand that it’s the right time.

“I swear that I always gave my all – not just in the last few years when we won everything, but before that, too.

“I always fought and gave everything for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you proud to be Argentinian through football.

“There’s not much time left and chapters are closing, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, loved, and will always love being on the national team.

“I’ve given everything I have; I have nothing more to give and, besides, there are some great young players coming up behind me who deserve to be there.

“Thank you for all the love and support over these 20 years. I’m going to miss hearing you all from the inside so much.

“Now I’m going to be just one of you, cheering and supporting you from the sidelines (in good times and bad, even more so).

“Thank you to my family for always being there, for accompanying me on this beautiful but difficult journey.

“Thank you to each and every one of the coaches, teammates and managers I had the privilege of working with. I take with me unforgettable memories and moments.

“I leave with the peace and pride of having given you, along with my teammates, dreamlike moments. It was incredible to have experienced it with you all. I love you.

“Thank you, God, for making me Argentinian. Go Argentina!

“I wrote these words on July 21st, two days after the final. Today, after [my father’s death], I’m even more convinced than before.”

Bradley Barcola eyes ‘very big things’ after joining Liverpool

Liverpool have signed France forward Bradley Barcola

Last Update:

Bradley Barcola says winning the Premier League is “one of my biggest dreams in my life” after joining Liverpool for £123 million.

The Reds have signed the 23-year-old on a long-term contract as part of a deal worth £106m plus £17m in potential add-ons.

“It took a long time but I’m really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play,” Barcola told Liverpool.

“I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League – it’s one of my biggest dreams in my life.

Table of Contents

How Bradley Barcola could be Mohamed Salah replacement

Barcola had two years remaining on his PSG contract but made it clear he would not extend his stay with the reigning European champions and was excluded from their Ligue 1 opener against Rennes, which ended in a 2-2 draw.

Barcola predominantly operates on the left wing but can play on the opposite flank. He faced competition for places from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue last season and was often used from the bench during the latter stages of PSG’s Champions League triumph.

Barcola made 49 appearances in all competitions during 2025/26, contributing 13 goals and seven assists as PSG retained the Ligue 1 title and continued their success in Europe.

The Lyon academy product registered 39 goals and 37 assists in 152 appearances for his former club.

Barcola also played a major role for France at the 2026 World Cup, featuring in all eight of their matches and scoring three goals.

The move could also have consequences for Cody Gakpo, who has been linked with Tottenham throughout the summer and has attracted interest from Manchester City.

Liverpool identified Barcola as their leading target to replace the prolific Mohamed Salah, who left Anfield at the end of last season.

articles.summary: Forest praised Daniel Munoz's 'mentality and ambition'
articles.content:
Forest sign Palace defender Munoz for up to £22m

Forest praised Daniel Munoz's 'mentality and ambition'

Last Update:

Daniel Munoz has called Nottingham Forest a “winning club” after being reunited with manager Oliver Glasner.

Full-back Munoz, who won the Conference League with Glasner at Crystal Palace last season, has joined Forest from the Eagles in a deal potentially worth £22 million.

The 30-year-old Colombia international has signed a three-year contract with an optional extra year.

Table of Contents

Daniel Munoz transfer: What full-back said

“I’m really excited because I can see so much talent,” Munoz told Forest’s website. “Forest is a team with great players, great qualities and great skills on the pitch.

“I can’t wait to get out there so I can help my new teammates… we’re going to do great things.

“The first thing is that this is a winning club. When this is the expectation and the mentality – both for the management and the technical team and for the players – this makes it special.

“It is a club that’s fought hard in recent years, it has competed hard, it got to the semi-finals of the Europa League [last season] and it has even greater objectives for the future.

“Really, this is what I like about Forest. That’s why I decided to come here.”

Nottingham Forest on Daniel Munoz transfer

Forest Chief Football Officer George Syrianos said Munoz had “consistently demonstrated his quality at the highest level”.

“Daniel has performed strongly in the Premier League and in European competition,” added Syrianos. “We believe he has the mentality and ambition to make a significant contribution.”

A 2-2 draw at Liverpool – twice being pegged back by the hosts – gave Forest their first positive result of the season on Saturday, having lost at home to Leeds United in the Premier League and EFL Cup.

Munoz could make his debut at home to Tottenham, who are yet to earn a point, on Saturday (15:00 BST).

The window opened on Monday June 15 and will shut on Tuesday September 1.

The deal sheet must arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes.

There are slight variations between the major European leagues. Here’s when they shut.

The Premier League winter transfer window opens on Friday January 1, 2027 and closes on Monday February 1, 2027 at 23:00 BST.

Clubs can only add players outside of transfer windows who are free agents and if they have room in their 25-man squad.

This means there is usually little to no movement when the window closes, with four months to wait until the window re-opens.

Sarr played a role in the move for the only goal of the game as Spurs beat Manchester United in the 2024/25 Europa League final. Here are some of his key stats for the club.

Tottenham transfer news: Pape Matar Sarr requested move

Man City pay Palmeiras £34m for ‘big addition’ Allan

Manchester City have praised Allan Elias' 'superb attitude'

Last Update:

Allan Elias has called his transfer to Manchester City from Palmeiras “surreal” after joining the Premier League leaders from Brazilian side Palmeiras for £34 million.

City have paid £32 million with a potential £2.2m in add-ons for the 22-year-old right-sided wideman, who has signed a five-year deal and could replace Savio, who joined Tottenham for £75m last week.

“Manchester City, with everything they have won over the past 15 years, are one of the most attractive clubs in the world for players,” Elias told City.

“To be able to sit here today and say I have joined them is the proudest moment of my life.”

Table of Contents

Allan Elias transfer: Winger on Manchester City

“I love Palmeiras and always will,” Elias said of the club he joined as a youth-team player in 2019 before breaking through in 2025.

“But the decision to come to City was an easy one. I want to be the best footballer I can be and the conversations I’ve had with the people at City so far have convinced me there isn’t a better place for me to fulfil my ambitions.

“I want to promise the Manchester City fans I will give absolutely everything to make the most of this opportunity.

“Now the hard work begins. I will give 100% in training and make the best case possible to the manager I should be playing.

“My intention is to help City continue winning trophies. If I can do that, it would be a dream come true.”

Allan Elias stats: Palmeiras goals, assists

City say the prospect comes from the “surfing paradise” of Florianopolis in southern Brazil and started playing futsal at the age of seven before joining Club Figueirense as a 14-year-old.

Having contributed 17 goals and four assists for Palmeiras’ under-20s, Allan became a first-team regular and played an important role in their comeback from 3-0 behind after the first leg of their Copa Libertadores tie against LDU Quito last season, providing an assist and winning the decisive penalty.

After losing the first leg 3-0 in Ecuador, Palmeiras pulled off a stunning 4-0 win with Allan setting up the opener for Ramon Sosa before being fouled in the dying minutes for the match-winning penalty.

Allan started the final, playing for 72 minutes in a 1-0 defeat to Flamengo. Here are some of his key stats.

Man City transfers: Allan ‘superb’

Hugo Viana called Allan “really exciting”. “We think he will be a big addition to the squad,” added City’s Director of Football.

“He has shown throughout his short career that he will fight to be the best he can be. Coming to Manchester and taking on the challenge of being a City player is another example of that.

“We watched his progress in Brazil and saw a player who thrives in the big moments and works hard for the team with a superb attitude.

“Everyone is very happy that he has joined us and we look forward to seeing him grow.”

City have beaten Bournemouth 2-1 at home and Crystal Palace 4-1 away in their opening fixtures. They host Coventry City on Saturday (15:00 BST).

articles.title: Carrick hails United’s mentality after Ipswich thrashing
articles.summary: Michael Carrick has hailed Manchester United for their comeback against Ipswich.
articles.content:
Carrick hails United’s mentality after Ipswich thrashing

Michael Carrick has hailed Manchester United for their comeback against Ipswich.

Last Update:

Michael Carrick said the mentality his side showed after going behind was the most pleasing aspect of Manchester United’s 5-2 win over Ipswich.

Bruno Fernandes’ hat-trick, Bryan Mbeumo’s sublime chip and a Jacob Greaves own goal gave United a resounding win, but Carrick was keen to focus on the character shown after Leif Davis’ early opener.

“The biggest pleasing thing for me was about dealing with setbacks, if you want to be a good team or a successful team,” Carrick said.

“Every team gets beat, or has to deal with setbacks in certain ways. We spoke about before the game to try and overcome last week, and we took a mini setback going a goal behind.

“The stubbornness, the belief, the confidence, the togetherness the boys showed at that stage was really pleasing for me. That mentality is what we relied on today.”

Fernandes inevitably dominated the post-match conversation, but Carrick was equally keen to highlight the performance of Kobbie Mainoo, who was outstanding in his first start of the season.

“I understand Bruno getting a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team,” he said. “On today’s performance, not much to improve. He was very, very good for a first start back.”

Fernandes given flowers

On Fernandes himself Carrick was equally direct. “It doesn’t surprise me. It’s just the kind of thing that gets labelled when you lose games.

“Just because you lose a game, it doesn’t mean everything’s wrong, or the wheels have come off, or they don’t want to play, or they’re not passionate or they’re not leaders. The best teams lose games of football. Together, the boys bounced back particularly well from different setbacks, and that will stand us in good stead moving forward.”

Marcus Rashford’s return to the starting line-up, his first Premier League start at Old Trafford in almost two years, also drew warm words from the United manager.

Rashford had been strongly linked with a move to Barcelona over the summer before remaining at the club. “He’s one of our own, he’s living his dream playing here now and trying to be successful and win,” Carrick said.

“I think there’s players that have gone and come back sometimes and maybe players that were going to leave but didn’t. It’s all about what you do next and what your intentions are, and he’s been fantastic since he came back. It was great to see him out on the pitch today.”

articles.content:
Alonso hails ‘valuable’ Chelsea win over Brighton but sweats on Caicedo injury

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso enjoyed his side's win over Brighton and has given an update on the fitness of Moises Caicedo.

Last Update:

Xabi Alonso described Chelsea’s 4-3 win over Brighton as a valuable three points, while confirming that Moises Caicedo will be assessed after the midfielder was forced off in the second half.

Chelsea were in complete control for large portions of the contest, racing into a three-goal lead through Romeo Lavia’s first Chelsea goal, Pedro Neto and Joao Pedro.

Brighton hit back with goals from Malick Yalcouye and an own goal from Joao Pedro to make it nervy, but Cole Palmer’s curling effort from 20 yards restored the Blues’ advantage and ultimately proved the winner, despite a late Pascal Gross consolation.

“All the wins I enjoy a lot, but it was a game that in different moments had different feelings,” Alonso said in his post-match press conference.

“In the end, we’re happy with the result. We value this win against a very good opponent who have been tough in the last few years.

“We are happy with that, and there are things and moments that we have done well, but it’s a process to keep on learning and improving. Usually, that is easier with a win.”

The afternoon was soured by Caicedo’s fitness setback. The Ecuador international had missed Chelsea’s opening two fixtures but was introduced from the bench midway through the second half, only to be replaced by Valentin Barco just 13 minutes later.

“He was cautious to stop and say his feeling wasn’t the best,” Alonso said when asked about the injury. “We need to assess during the week, but it wasn’t something new.”

The result means Chelsea have made it two wins from two in the Premier League, with Alonso making clear there is still plenty of room for improvement despite the positive start.

articles.content:
Premier League round-up: Calvert-Lewin rescues Leeds at Brentford as Sunderland edge Fulham

Catch up with the best of the action from the Premier League on Sunday.

Last Update:

Table of Contents

Brentford 1-1 Leeds

Dominic Calvert-Lewin rescued Leeds a point at the Gtech Community Stadium, heading home in the 82nd minute to cancel out Kevin Schade’s effort and earn Daniel Farke’s side a share of the spoils.

Brentford had controlled much of the second half and looked to have done enough when Schade struck in the 70th minute, the midfielder’s effort taking a deflection off Jaka Bijol on its way past James Trafford.

Andrews had introduced Rico Henry and Mikkel Damsgaard just before the hour and the combination of the two immediately gave Brentford a different dimension, with the pair combining to create the opening goal.

Farke responded by turning to Wilfried Gnonto and Brenden Aaronson from the bench, and Gnonto provided the decisive contribution with a whipped cross from the left that Calvert-Lewin met with a clean header from six yards.

Brentford were missing Mathias Jenson through injury and Yehor Yarmolyuk, who has been managing a disrupted pre-season, while Gabriel Gudmundsson only returned to full training last week after a hamstring problem and featured briefly late on for Leeds.

Sunderland 1-0 Fulham

Wilson Isidor came off the bench to score the only goal and give Sunderland their first win of the season at the Stadium of Light, with Chris Rigg also making an appearance from the bench to give the home crowd something to cheer in what was Regis Le Bris’s first home Premier League match of the campaign.

Sunderland had lost their opener 2-1 at Ipswich and desperately needed a response in front of their own supporters.

Isidor, introduced as a substitute for Brian Brobbey, provided exactly that, finishing to give Le Bris the three points his side needed to calm early-season nerves.

Fulham, under Alvaro Arbeloa in his first Premier League management role, showed enough attacking intent to suggest they will not be far from goals as the season develops.

Teenage midfielder Josh King was lively throughout and Gonzalo Garcia, who scored on his debut in the League Cup against Wimbledon in midweek, offered a focal point up front.

But the Cottagers could not find a way past Sunderland’s well-organised defensive block and are yet to take a point.

articles.title: MLS: Messi scores four as Inter Miami end winless run
articles.summary: It was a big win for Lionel Messi and Inter Miami on Saturday night.
articles.content:
MLS: Messi scores four as Inter Miami end winless run

It was a big win for Lionel Messi and Inter Miami on Saturday night.

Last Update:

Lionel Messi scored four times as Inter Miami ended their recent winless run with a record-breaking 7-1 win over CF Montreal on Saturday.

The result saw Miami score more goals in a single match than ever before, with Messi putting on another memorable display to fire his side back to winning ways.

The Argentine opened the scoring in the 40th minute when his free kick took a deflection on its way into the net.

Messi doubled Miami’s advantage seven minutes after half-time following a brilliant solo run, before turning provider for Luis Suarez to make it 3-0.

He then completed his hat trick with seven minutes of normal time remaining, delicately lifting the ball over the goalkeeper.

Messi still had time to add another.

Deep into stoppage time, the 39-year-old stepped up for another free kick and curled the ball into the side of the net with his usual precision.

“That’s what it means to have Messi on the team,” Miami midfielder Casemiro told Apple TV. “We have to enjoy these moments because he is a person, a player that makes history.

“We saw today that we have to enjoy it, keep supporting and keep competing with him because he continues to be the best. He proved it in the World Cup. We have to enjoy it because, with him, we are so much stronger.”

Messi still making history

The four-goal haul was the eighth time Messi has scored at least four goals in a match during his career, but the first since joining Inter Miami.

His previous four-goal performance came in February 2020, when he found the net four times for Barcelona against Eibar in LaLiga.

Messi has also become the fastest player in MLS history to record 20 multigoal games in the regular season, reaching the mark in just 72 appearances.

The veteran forward now leads the MLS scoring charts with 18 goals from 19 matches this season, two clear of FC Dallas striker Petar Musa.

“There are no words to describe such footballing beauty,” Miami coach Guillermo Hoyos said. “So much is going on that words simply fall short.

“He is constantly looking for that goal, that play, that pass; I don’t think he’s an ordinary footballer. Analysing him, both as a player and as a person, goes so deep that you run out of words.”

The victory was Miami’s first in MLS since July 25 and ended a five-game winless run in all competitions, including the Leagues Cup.

The hosts added a seventh goal through 18-year-old Alexander Shaw in the 89th minute.

The win keeps Inter Miami second in the Eastern Conference, although they remain 10 points behind Nashville SC.

articles.title: De Zerbi ‘will not panic’ despite Tottenham’s winless Premier League start
articles.summary: Tottenham are bottom of the Premier League with two defeats from two after losing to Newcastle, but their manager is staying calm.
articles.content:
De Zerbi ‘will not panic’ despite Tottenham’s winless Premier League start

Tottenham are bottom of the Premier League with two defeats from two after losing to Newcastle, but their manager is staying calm.

Last Update:

Roberto De Zerbi insisted Tottenham will not panic after his side slipped to a second successive Premier League defeat to start the season, losing 2-0 at home to Newcastle United.

Tottenham have spent over £300million in the transfer window in an effort to drastically improve a team that finished 17th in each of the previous two campaigns, their marquee signing a £100million deal to prise Sandro Tonali from Newcastle.

Spurs will have been hopeful of getting off the mark against the Magpies, having bounced back from a dismal 3-0 defeat to Brentford in their opening game with a 5-1 win over Championship pace-setters Charlton Athletic in the EFL Cup.

But, after failing to take several chances in the first half, Spurs were undone by an excellent second-half showing from Newcastle, who prevailed thanks to strikes from Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa, with Tonali withdrawn to the delight of the travelling fans shortly after the second goal.

Despite failing to score in each of their first two games, De Zerbi is preaching calm after a game he felt they were unfortunate not to win.

He told Sky Sports: “I think for 65 minutes we played better than Newcastle, we had a chance to score and didn’t score. And then after the goal we lost the distances.

“We created other chances but if you analyse the game, we had more chances, more shots, we are not a team yet and have to improve on a lot of things but that is normal for a new team.

“Forget the result. I am not angry, we are working well and were unlucky today with the result.

“We had more control of the ball, we can improve in the defensive phase with the distances. Sometimes we regained the ball and had chances to score and also with the ball we can improve and keep it much better, but it is part of this work when you change many players and start a new project with a new team.”

“We will not panic. I know very well where we are going, what the plan is and what difficult problems we could find in our way.

“I am sorry for the fans and sorry for the players for the result but we have to improve and to change two seasons like the last two is impossible in 10 days and with people in the transfer market.

“We have to work hard on the pitch and find the connection with the players because last season before the end of the season we were in the Championship and we stayed up together.

“Now we have to keep clam and focus on improvement. We have a great squad and great players, we can’t use all the players we brought but if we work in this way and believe in ourselves I think we will change the last two seasons.

“If the rush is more important than the journey we can’t find the solutions to the last two seasons.”

articles.title: Wissa hails Jaissle as Newcastle’s ‘best signing’ after Magpies continue unbeaten start
articles.summary: The Magpies look rejuvenated under their new manager.
articles.content:
Wissa hails Jaissle as Newcastle’s ‘best signing’ after Magpies continue unbeaten start

The Magpies look rejuvenated under their new manager.

Last Update:

Yoane Wissa hailed manager Matthias Jaissle as Newcastle’s best signing after they claimed their first Premier League win under their new boss with a 2-0 victory at Tottenham.

Jaissle was denied a win in his opening game as Liverpool claimed a point at St James’ Park with a last-gasp penalty but, after beating West Brom 3-2 in the EFL Cup in midweek, the German saw his maiden league triumph come via an excellent away performance.

Anthony Elanga broke the deadlock with a fine finish on the turn shortly after the hour mark, with Wissa doubling the lead 10 minutes later with a wonderfully improvised finish from Nick Woltemade’s knock down.

Table of Contents

Wissa hails Jaissle impact

Elanga and Wissa have each enjoyed superb starts to the new season after struggling last campaign following big-money moves from Nottingham Forest and Brentford respectively.

Their form has helped Newcastle make an unbeaten start to the new season despite the departures of three key players in Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, who left for Tottenham in a £100million move but failed to make a tangible impact against his former club.

And Wissa, whose first season on Tyneside was derailed by injury, was effusive in his praise of Jaissle when asked about Newcastle’s early success.

“I am very happy, to be part of the team and part of the club,” Wissa told Sky Sports. “The fans love their club and love the players and what they want is us to give them what we have. They never stopped singing or shouting so that is for them today.

“Of course we lost so many players but the club worked well. It is challenging and we need players to step up, like me for instance, I didn’t play last year and now I have a chance to play. So many players have to step up and enjoy the challenge and with the fans behind us nobody can stop us.

“I am not injured and I feel confident now. I trust myself and I trust the manager and even though I didn’t play last year I have trained a lot with the players and they know my movements.

“Eddie Howe did a top job and the new manager [Matthias Jaissle] came with a new identity and that [first goal] is something we have been working on. Every part of the game we are really precise. He is a really dynamic manager, so we have to give everything and I think he is the best signing of Newcastle so far.”

Jaissle: Newcastle ‘DNA’ key to strong start

Jaissle, meanwhile, gave subtle praise to predecessor Howe —  who left the club last month after a celebrated five-year spell — indicating that the foundations he laid have made his job in the opening weeks easier.

“We are really proud as a club and coaching staff to see the team delivering on the pitch and also seeing players committed to what we are doing,” Jaissle told Sky. “Proud and a moment to enjoy.

“We did well also last week. It was a step in the right direction again with a strong opponent, huge signings. The way we handled the opponent was amazing.

“The DNA of Newcastle is a good fit to the playing style I like to see so therefore we saw already in the past similarities.”

Asked about the improvements made by Elanga and Wissa, he replied: “I don’t take the compliments yet. I try just to encourage them, motivate them and support them, not only those two but the whole squad. I am really happy to see the improvement.

“It [the first league win] means a lot. I just said to the lads in the locker room we can count now our defensive stability. The clean sheet today was a big goal.”

Newcastle are reported to be looking at multiple forwards in the closing days of the transfer window, having signed seven players so far.

“We have ambitions, we know what is needed,” Jaissle said on that subject. “The squad is strong but there are still a couple of days left then we can talk again.”

articles.title: Liverpool have lessons to learn after Forest draw, says boss Iraola
articles.summary: The Reds needed a late equaliser for the second game in a row
articles.content:
Liverpool have lessons to learn after Forest draw, says boss Iraola

The Reds needed a late equaliser for the second game in a row

Last Update:

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said his side must learn to play with more intensity after the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest in the Premier League.

Iraola was indebted to a late equaliser for a second week in a row and witnessed a sloppy and at times disjointed performance at Anfield.

A fine late goal from Victor Munoz preserved a point but the former Bournemouth manager was left with plenty to work on.

He told BBC Match of the Day: “We were poor in the first half. We improved a lot our performance in the second half, we came from behind twice, but I think the first half didn’t allow us to win the game at the end.

“We were quite passive without the ball. We were allowing them to pass and both goals, which came from throw-ins, we didn’t defend properly. The general feeling is that we were passive defensively.

“In the second half when we were more aggressive and played with more intensity we attacked better. I hope this serves as a lesson for the future.

“Victor [Munoz] has played really well. Defensively and offensively he did a very good job and was always a threat.”

‘I am proud of the performance’

Forest manager Oliver Glasner was close to his first win in charge of the club but left Anfield in positive mood.

Forest lost back-to-back games against Leeds last week in league and cup but were much better at Anfield, with Morgan Gibbs-White’s penalty almost giving them a win.

He told BBC Match of the Day: “I think we all have the same feeling, proud of the performance, proud of how many chances we created and proud of the reaction after we conceded the equaliser.

“On the other side, we’re all a little bit disappointed we couldn’t get the win. I think this shows how good we performed, how well we played. Overall, a very good performance.

“I could see our tactical shape work well in many parts but after 60-65 minutes, the level drops a little bit. Which shows that everything is not 100% settled, it can’t be after six or seven weeks together. Also, we conceded the same goal more or less, in the same area.

“What I loved most was how we played forward and created the chances, especially in the first half. I think we should have led by more than one goal.

“But again, it’s still the beginning of the season. The beginning of the journey and this performance will give us confidence.

“I always hope the next time it will go quicker but, again, we could see many positive aspects. Many things that should and will give us confidence but it’s important to stay humble and keep working hard.”

articles.title: Liverpool agree to pay £123m to sign Bradley Barcola from PSG – reports
articles.summary: The France forward is on his way to the Premier League
articles.content:
Liverpool agree to pay £123m to sign Bradley Barcola from PSG – reports

The France forward is on his way to the Premier League

Last Update:

Liverpool will pay up to £123m to sign Paris Saint-Germain forward Bradley Barcola.

The move has been close to being finalised all week with the latest reports now saying he will have a medical this weekend.

PSG initially valued the France attacker at £145m, but the Reds have now reportedly agreed a package worth an initial £106m with £17m in potential add-ons.

The forward will sign a five-year deal.

The move could also have consequences for Cody Gakpo, who has been linked with Tottenham throughout the summer and has also attracted interest from Manchester City.

Liverpool identified Barcola as their leading target to replace Mohamed Salah earlier in the summer, with the club preparing an opening offer for the France international in July.

Salah replacement

The 23-year-old has two years remaining on his PSG contract but has made it clear that he does not intend to extend his stay with the European champions.

He was subsequently left out of PSG’s squad for their Ligue 1 opener against Rennes, which ended in a 2-2 draw.

Barcola predominantly operates on the left wing but can also play on the opposite flank. He faced competition for places from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue last season and was often used from the bench during the latter stages of PSG’s Champions League campaign.

Despite that competition, Barcola made 49 appearances in all competitions during the 2025-26 season, scoring 13 goals and providing seven assists as PSG retained the Ligue 1 title and continued their success in Europe.

Since breaking into the first team, the Lyon academy product has registered 39 goals and 37 assists in 152 appearances for the club.

Barcola also played a major role for France at this summer’s World Cup, featuring in all eight matches and scoring three goals.

articles.title: Maresca hails Cherki after dominant Manchester City win
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca has spoken after Manchester City's win over Crystal Palace.
articles.content:
Maresca hails Cherki after dominant Manchester City win

Enzo Maresca has spoken after Manchester City's win over Crystal Palace.

Last Update:

Enzo Maresca insisted Manchester City’s opening difficulties at Selhurst Park only made the 4-1 win more pleasing, as the City manager lavished praise on Rayan Cherki.

Two goals from Cherki and a brace from Erling Haaland sealed a comfortable win on a night that started awkwardly before City found their rhythm.

“Probably the first five or 10 minutes we saw how difficult it was,” he said. “It’s a difficult pitch and tough opponents. After 10 minutes we controlled the game on the ball and off the ball and deserved to win.

“The intensity on the team has been good. We scored four, probably could’ve scored more, only conceded one. Off the ball we were quite good, struggled for the first 10 minutes. On the ball, tried to put players into a position to attack.”

Table of Contents

Cherki singled out for defensive display

While the Frenchman’s two goals and two assists drew the headlines, Maresca was particularly vocal about the work Cherki produced when City did not have the ball, specifically his role in nullifying Adam Wharton.

“His performance off the ball was unbelievable,” Maresca said. “Everyone knows his quality but when he works hard off the ball, he was in charge of Wharton, he controlled him. He was very good.

“He’s helping us and is going to help in the future. We know he’s a quality player. I think he was very, very good off the ball and was working very hard.”

Foden adaptation continues

Foden again drew mixed reviews from those watching, missing several clear chances in the first half before contributing two assists.

Maresca struck a patient tone when discussing a player he clearly sees as central to his plans, while acknowledging that the winger role is not where Foden is most comfortable.

“In the last 10-15 minutes you can see he was even more happy to play inside behind Erling. That’s his position. He’s trying to adapt and trying to help when playing winger. His working is good, he’s doing very good,” he added

“He’s adapting, we know he’s not a winger, we’re trying to find a solution. When he was inside, you could see he was enjoying it more. The attitude is very good and it’s what we need.”

articles.title: Aston Villa complete £65m signing of Nicolas Jackson
articles.summary: Nicolas Jackson is Aston Villa's latest summer signing.
articles.content:
Aston Villa complete £65m signing of Nicolas Jackson

Nicolas Jackson is Aston Villa's latest summer signing.

Last Update:

Aston Villa have completed the signing of Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea in a deal worth up to £65 million, with Unai Emery confirming the Senegal international will lead Villa’s attack as the club prepares for life without Ollie Watkins.

Jackson, 25, has signed at Villa Park after Chelsea agreed an initial fee of £47.5 million, with add-ons potentially taking the total to £65 million.

He becomes the third major piece of business between Villa and Chelsea this summer, following Morgan Rogers’ club-record £117 million departure to Stamford Bridge in June and Alejandro Garnacho’s subsequent loan move in the other direction.

The arrival of Jackson directly paves the way for Watkins to complete his move to Al Hilal, with Fabrizio Romano confirming the Saudi Pro League side have agreed a deal worth €58.4 million plus add-ons for the England international.

Jackson brings with him a profile Emery knows well. The pair worked together at Villarreal, where Jackson made his senior breakthrough before a £32 million move to Chelsea in 2023.

He went on to score 30 goals in 81 appearances for the Blues before spending last season on loan at Bayern Munich, where he registered 11 goals in 34 appearances, including three in the Champions League, and contributed to the Bundesliga and DFB Pokal double.

Jackson could be available for Monday’s trip to the Emirates Stadium to face Arsenal, though Emery will assess his fitness having been largely absent from first-team training at Chelsea in recent weeks.

Leon Goretzka, who completed his free transfer from Bayern Munich on Thursday, is also in contention to make his Villa debut in what is already shaping up as a defining early-season fixture for a club that were beaten 4-0 by Brighton on opening day.

articles.title: Villa agree £47m deal for PSG winger Mbaye
articles.summary: The teenager will give Villa versatility on the wings.
articles.content:
Villa agree £47m deal for PSG winger Mbaye

The teenager will give Villa versatility on the wings.

Last Update:

Aston Villa have reportedly agreed a deal in principle to sign Paris Saint-Germain winger Ibrahim Mbaye.

The Athletic’s David Ornstein reported that the two clubs have come to terms on a deal worth €55million (£47m) for the 18-year-old Senegal international, who established himself in PSG’s first team last season.

Having made 12 appearances and scored one goal in 2024-25, the PSG academy product played in 29 games in all competitions last season, scoring three goals, one of which came in the 2-0 win over Lens that sealed the Ligue 1 title for Luis Enrique’s men.

Mbaye also found the net for Senegal against France at this summer’s World Cup, which the Lions of Teranga exited in the round of 32.

He was an unused substitute as PSG came from behind to beat Villa 2-1 in the UEFA Super Cup this month, winning that competition for a second successive year.

Now Mbaye will leave PSG having won two Ligue 1 titles, two Champions League crowns, the Coupe de France and the FIFA Intercontinental Cup.

His arrival will give Villa a versatile option on the flanks, with Mbaye able to play on both the right and the left. Villa had shown interest in signing Rafael Leao from AC Milan, but the Portugal international is instead closing in on a move to Galatasaray.

Mbaye’s signing will take the number of Villa additions up to 10 in a transfer window that has seen much of the team that finished fourth in the Premier League and won the Europa League last season dismantled.

Villa have seen Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne leave the club, with goalkeeper Emi Martinez set to join Chelsea and striker Ollie Watkins poised to make the move to Saudi side Al Hilal. Watkins is set to be replaced by Nicolas Jackson, who has agreed to join Villa from Chelsea.

Villa boss reveals emotional Watkins farewell

Despite Watkins refusing to play in Villa’s 4-0 defeat to Brighton and Hove Albion last Sunday, manager Unai Emery revealed he said an emotional goodbye to the England international this week.

“I can tell you now Watkins, his commitment and his behaviour was fantastic,” said Emery ahead of Monday’s clash with Arsenal.

“We didn’t get a deal to finish his last match playing at Brighton, but he told us after the match he was sorry and he told us as well he made a mistake.

“He was wrong but we accepted it. The players as well because he always had very good behaviour and commitment with the club, with us and with me.

“For me, it’s a fantastic guy, a fantastic guy even more than a player. I told him bye with a huge hug and with small tears.

“But now it’s a new chapter here with Nicolas Jackson and we replace him.”

articles.title: ‘It is very important they feel desire to play’ – Alonso speaks on Enzo Fernandez absence from Chelsea cup tie
articles.summary: Alonso suggested Fernandez was not in the right frame of mind.
articles.content:
‘It is very important they feel desire to play’ – Alonso speaks on Enzo Fernandez absence from Chelsea cup tie

Alonso suggested Fernandez was not in the right frame of mind.

Last Update:

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso indicated Enzo Fernandez did not have the desire to play in their EFL Cup tie with Luton Town as speculation around a move to Manchester City persists.

Alonso said ahead of Thursday’s 2-0 win over League One Luton that he expected Fernandez to feature, having come off the bench in their Premier League opener, a 3-2 win over Fulham, on Monday.

But Fernandez was not included in the squad and, speaking ahead of Sunday’s clash with Brighton and Hove Albion at Stamford Bridge, Alonso gave a clear suggestion that Fernandez was not in the right frame of mind to play.

“I said we need the players that are in the best situation to play,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference.

“We need to take everything into consideration – players that are in a good moment, players that are not feeling that energy to play.

“For me, it is very important they feel this desire to play and to have good preparation.

“We [Alonso and Fernandez] talked and we decided for tonight it was better not to be part of the squad. He is a top player.”

Former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca is keen to lure Fernandez to the Etihad Stadium as the final piece of City’s midfield revamp.

Chelsea had set a deadline of last Friday for City to sign the Argentina international. However, they are still said to be open to a sale if they get at least £120million and are able to sign a replacement.

Asked if Fernandez would need to replaced were he to make the move City, Alonso replied: “We have been talking about speculation, sorry, but I’m not the one who talks too early.

“We will see what happens. We want to be ready always.”

Chelsea this week sold striker Liam Delap to Nottingham Forest for £50million, but are set to make Atalanta centre-back Honest Anahor their 11th signing of the summer.

“We are quite close to the plan we had,” Alonso said of his side’s transfer business.

“We will see where we finish, if it’s fully executed or there are things still to be done or things we couldn’t do. But for sure I think overall the balance of what we have is going to be good. We have to see how the last few days develop. But so far the team is coming together.

“It is a process that will take time. We are in a good position, with a few more days to see.”

articles.title: Carrick hopeful of Baleba Man United debut before international break
articles.summary: The midfielder has an ankle injury that will keep him out for at least a couple of weeks.
articles.content:
Carrick hopeful of Baleba Man United debut before international break

The midfielder has an ankle injury that will keep him out for at least a couple of weeks.

Last Update:

Manchester United are hopeful midfielder Carlos Baleba will be able to make his debut for the club before the September international break, but manager Michael Carrick refused to put any deadlines on his recovery from an ankle injury.

Baleba this week completed a £70million move to Old Trafford from Brighton and Hove Albion.

The Cameroon international’s arrival should significantly boost the United midfield by bringing some much-needed physicality to the engine room.

But United will have to wait a little while before they can reap the benefits of his signing because of his injury, which is expected to keep him on the sideline for at least two more weeks.

Domestic football takes a significant break next month, with the next international break stretching from September 21 to October 6.

Should Baleba fail to return before the break, his United debut will likely come on October 10 when they host Tottenham.

But Carrick does not see Baleba’s lay-off as a significant problem.

“He’s got a little ankle issue,” Carrick told his pre-match press conference ahead of the visit of newly promoted Ipswich Town.

“So, maybe a couple of weeks or so, maybe three weeks, we’ll see. But we knew that before, so it’s no major issue. It’ll be great to have him back when we can.

“We’re delighted to have Carlos. He has huge potential, he’s a really exciting signing or us, the quality he has, the attributes he has offset the balance of the group we’ve got.

“Different strengths, different combinations. So much more to come from him as well, so it’s exciting for us.”

United are also without Amad Diallo after the Ivorian sustained a knock in training, with Carrick unsure if either he or Baleba will be available before club football takes an extended pause.

“It’s obviously new, you know, having the break to deal with,” Carrick added.

“But we’ll wait and see. We’ll wait and see. We’re hopeful, but I don’t want to put any deadlines on it just yet.”

articles.title: ‘Anything can be reversed’ – Simeone vows to make Alvarez feel important as Atletico forward misses Sevilla clash
articles.summary: Alvarez will miss the game with Sevilla as his transfer saga rumbles on.
articles.content:
‘Anything can be reversed’ – Simeone vows to make Alvarez feel important as Atletico forward misses Sevilla clash

Alvarez will miss the game with Sevilla as his transfer saga rumbles on.

Last Update:

Diego Simeone has vowed to make Julian Alvarez “feel as important as he has always been” when he returns to the Atletico Madrid squad.

Alvarez will be absent as Atletico face Sevilla on Saturday as the saga around his desire to join Barcelona rumbles on, with reports in Spain claiming he has submitted a medical report to the club stating he is dealing with depression.

The Argentina international was booed and walked straight down the tunnel at full-time of Atletico’s LaLiga opener, a 2-2 draw with Villarreal, having come on as a second-half substitute.

Atletico this week responded to comments from Barca president Joan Laporta by stating there is a “0% chance” of him being sold to the defending LaLiga champions, a stance the club’s board gave its unanimous approval on Thursday.

Alvarez has four years remaining on his Atletico contract and, with the club unwavering in their desire not to sell him to Barca, a move to Arsenal looks a more likely exit route for the former Manchester City forward.

But the possibility of Alvarez leaving does not appear to be on Simeone’s mind, with the Atletico boss clearly planning on having him in the team after the transfer window closes next week.

“I understand that most of the questions will be about Julian,” Simeone said at his pre-match press conference.

“The club was firm and clear in everything they explained and regarding what is going to happen. My stance remains the same: from a sporting perspective, I hope to help him in the best possible way so he can continue to be the vital player he is for us, while I focus on my own task at hand, which is Sevilla.

“Obviously, Julian won’t be available tomorrow, and we have to compete against an opponent coming off two wins and riding high on confidence; we need to steer the match in a direction where we think we can do some damage.

“When Julian returns to training, I’ll do everything possible to make him feel as important as he has always been.”

While the Atletico fans’ response to Alvarez would suggest the situation between him and the club cannot be salvaged, Simeone has a very different view.

He added: “In life, anything can be reversed as long as there is health.”

articles.title: When is the Conference League draw 2026/27? Date, time, league phase schedule, TV channel and live stream
articles.summary: All you need to know about this season's Conference League
articles.content:
When is the Conference League draw 2026/27? Date, time, league phase schedule, TV channel and live stream

All you need to know about this season's Conference League

Last Update:

The draw for the 2026/27 edition of the Conference League will schedule the league phase as teams from across Europe bid to succeed Crystal Palace as champions.

The Eagles beat Rayo Vallecano in the 2025/26 final to become the third Premier League club to win the competition after Chelsea in 2025 and West Ham in 2023.

Olympiacos won the 2023/2024 Conference League and Roma triumphed in the inaugural edition in 2021/22.

Here’s what you need to know about the Conference League draw, including when it takes place, when future draws are and the fixture schedule for 2024/25.

Table of Contents

When is the Conference League draw?

The draw will take place on Friday, August 28 – a day after the play-off ties come to a close to decide the last teams to qualify.

The draw ceremony will start at 12:00 BST / 07:00 ET / 04:00 PT.

How to watch Conference League draw: TV channel, online live stream

The draw will be shown live and for free on UEFA.com, as well as on UEFA’s YouTube channel.

TNT Sports will also broadcast the draw on TNT Sports 1 and the HBO Max app.

Conference League schedule, fixtures 2026/27

The league phase starts on October 15 and ends on December 17.

When is the Conference League knockout phase?

The play-offs are in February as part of a knockout phase lasting until June 2.

When are the Conference League draws?

The dates for the knockout phase draws were yet to be confirmed as of August 25, 2026.

Which English clubs are in the Conference League 2025/26?

Brighton & Hove Albion qualified for the Conference League by finishing seventh in last season’s Premier League.

The Seagulls must beat Norwegian side Tromso at home on August 27 to secure a place in the league phase, having drawn the first leg of their qualifying tie 0-0 away.

When is the Conference League final?

The final will take place on June 2 2027 at the Besiktas Park home of Turkish Super Lig side Besiktas in Istanbul.

The setting could be a good omen for English sides: Aston Villa beat Freiburg there to win last season’s Europa League final, seven years after European champions Liverpool beat Europa League holders Chelsea at the same stadium to lift the Super Cup trophy.

The winners gain a place in the league phase of the 2026/27 Europa League if they have not qualified through their domestic competition.

articles.title: When is the Europa League draw? Date, time, schedule, where to watch
articles.summary: English clubs have been in seven of the last 11 Europa League finals
articles.content:
When is the Europa League draw? Date, time, schedule, where to watch

English clubs have been in seven of the last 11 Europa League finals

Last Update:

The draw for the 2026/27 edition of the Europa League will schedule the initial eight matches as teams from across Europe bid to succeed Aston Villa as champions.

Villa beat Freiburg in the 2025/26 final, with Sevilla’s seven triumphs making the Spanish side by far the most successful team in Europa League history.

Premier League side Bournemouth are making their European debut this season after finishing sixth in the top flight, while Crystal Palace qualified by winning the Conference League.

Sunderland join them, making their second-ever appearance in Europe a season after winning promotion to the Premier League.

Table of Contents

When is the 2026 Europa League draw?

The draw will take place on Friday, August 28 – a day after the play-off ties come to a close to decide the last teams to qualify.

The draw will start at 12:00 BST / 07:00 ET / 04:00 PT.

How to watch Europa League draw: TV channel, live online stream

The draw will be shown live and for free on UEFA.com, as well as on UEFA’s YouTube channel.

TNT Sports will also broadcast the draw on TNT Sports 1 and the HBO Max app.

2026/27 Europa League format

In a change from the group stage held until 2023/24, each team now plays eight matches in the league phase, all against different opponents.

Four of those matches will be at home and four away, with the opponents determined according to four seeding pots split by rankings.

Teams will play two opponents from each of those pots – one against a team from each pot at home and one away. The results decide the overall standings in one league.

The top eight sides in the table qualify automatically for the round of 16. The teams finishing in ninth to 24th will compete in a two-legged knockout phase play-off to reach the last 16.

Teams finishing 25th or lower are out of Europe for the season.

Europa League schedule, fixtures 2026/27

The league phase starts on September 16 and runs until the end of January.

When is the Europa League knockout phase?

The knockout phase starts with the play-offs in February to reach the last 16.

When are the Europa League draws?

The dates for the knockout phase draws were yet to be confirmed as of August 25, 2026.

Which English clubs are in the Europa League 2026/27?

Under former head coach Andoni Iraola, Bournemouth finished sixth in last season’s Premier League with the help of an 18-match unbeaten league run to end an exceptional campaign.

Championship play-off winners the previous season, Sunderland won their final two matches of a superb season – part of a run of eight points from their closing four league games – to secure seventh.

Palace enjoyed a remarkable year in cup competitions, winning the FA Cup to reach the Conference League and triumphing in that competition with a 1-0 win over Spanish side Rayo Vallecano in the final.

When is the Europa League final?

The final will take place on May 26 2027 at Stadion Frankfurt.

articles.title: Everton ‘not in a hurry to sell our best players’, says Moyes amid Ndiaye Man City speculation
articles.summary: Everton are reported to value Ndiaye at £80million.
articles.content:
Everton ‘not in a hurry to sell our best players’, says Moyes amid Ndiaye Man City speculation

Everton are reported to value Ndiaye at £80million.

Last Update:

David Moyes insisted Everton are in no hurry to sell their best players amid speculation linking Iliman Ndiaye with Manchester City, and also refused to address talk of Jack Grealish returning to Merseyside.

Ndiaye has excelled for Everton since joining from Marseille in 2024, scoring 17 goals and providing four assists.

The winger has reportedly attracted interest from City after they sold Savio to Tottenham for an initial £75m, though Everton are said to value Ndiaye at £80million.

Asked about the speculation, Moyes indicated he does not fear imminently losing the Senegal international to their Premier League rivals.

“As far as I know, we’ve got nothing to be concerned about, we’ve had no contact from any club,” Moyes said in his press conference ahead of Everton’s trip to Bournemouth.

“Somebody told me we had contact with Al-Hilal during the summer, we had nothing from them. There’s a lot stuff that floats around which is not always true. Maybe this is true but certainly the stuff previous wasn’t.”

City attacking midfielder Grealish is said to be of interest to several Premier League clubs after he scored two goals and registered six assists while on loan at Everton last season.

But Moyes rejected the opportunity to talk about a potential return for the 30-year-old.

“I wouldn’t talk about individual players at other clubs,” Moyes added.

“Jack [Grealish] isn’t at our club. He was brilliant for us, great boy, but it’s wrong for me to talk about him if he’s at another club.

“We’re certainly not in a hurry to sell our best players, that’s for sure.”
